subject: [PATCH 2/3] fs/proc/task_mmu: don't read young/dirty from a non-present PMD in smaps

reviews.author: Lorenzo Stoakes (ARM)
reviews.summary: Identified a potential issue with non-present PMDs, but ultimately found the fix to be correct. Provided a Reviewed-by tag.

reviews.author: David Hildenbrand (Arm)
reviews.summary: Acknowledged the patch and provided an Acked-by tag.

2026-11-11.patch_summary: This patch fixes a bug in the /proc/PID/smaps code where it incorrectly reads young and dirty bits from non-present PMDs, leading to incorrect accounting of swap offsets. The fix involves only reading these bits when the PMD is present, which prevents garbage values from being used.

reviews.author: Baolin Wang
reviews.summary: Found the fix to be reasonable and provided a Reviewed-by tag.
reviews.raw_body:
On 11/11/26 7:38 PM, Usama Arif wrote:
> smaps_pmd_entry() passes pmd_young(*pmd) and pmd_dirty(*pmd) to
> smaps_account() for every PMD, including migration and device-private
> entries, where those bits hold part of the swap offset rather than
> accessed/dirty state. smaps_pte_entry() only reads them when the entry
> is present.
> 
> On x86_64 the offset is stored inverted across bits 9-58, which overlap
> _PAGE_SAVED_DIRTY, so pmd_dirty() returns garbage: a clean 2MB
> device-private mapping is accounted as 2048 kB dirty, and lazyfree
> accounting is suppressed. pgtable_64.h also warns that the hardware can
> set the accessed and dirty bits on non-present entries by mistake.
> 
> Only read the bits when the PMD is present.
> 
> Fixes: c94b6923fa0a ("/proc/PID/smaps: Add PMD migration entry parsing")
> Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
> Signed-off-by: Usama Arif <usama.arif@linux.dev>
> ---

Make sense to me.
Reviewed-by: Baolin Wang <baolin.wang@linux.alibaba.com>
